entities.summary: The church of Saint Mary at Mount Naranco is a pre-Romanesque Asturian building on the slope of Mount Naranco situated 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) from Oviedo, northern Spain. Ramiro I of Asturias ordered it to be built as a royal palace, part of a larger complex that also incorporated the nearby church of San Miguel de Lillo, 100 meters away. The palace was completed in 842 and had in part a religious function, being consecrated in 848. Its structural features, such as the barrel vault—with transverse ribs corresponding one-to-one with contraforts at the exterior, make it a clear precursor of the Romanesque construction.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a royal palace and precursor to Romanesque construction, Santa María del Naranjo played a significant role in shaping Asturian architecture during the 9th century. Its structural innovations influenced subsequent building designs across Southern Europe.
